item.title: US, S/Korea, Japan vow ‘complete’ N/Korea denuclearization
item.description: The United States, South Korea and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea on Saturday, as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible talks with Washington. Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization” of North Korea during talks on Friday on the sidelines of a Group of 20 (G20) meeting in Atlanta in the US state of Georgia, the US State Department said. They also pledged “full implementation” of UN Security Council resolutions, including a ban on supporting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea, which is backed by Russia and China, has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. – Open to meeting – Trump has made repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks, while scaling back joint military drills with ally South Korea. The mercurial US leader even bucked long-held US policy last year by conceding that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”, while reaching out to Pyongyang for talks, saying he was “100 percent” open to a meeting — a suggestion that went unanswered. Analysts and South Korea’s spy agency say Kim may have conveyed Pyongyang’s position on potential talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong. South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung — who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief. Critics have said such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal. Analysts say China may also be moving towards tacit acceptance, pointing to the omission of North Korean denuclearisation from statements after Kim and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in June. Pyongyang denounced a joint statement on Saturday by a group of nations monitoring sanctions implementations against it, vowing that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”. item.title: NYSC Members Kidnap: ‘I didn’t know passengers in my bus had AK-47 rifles – Driver tells court
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara One of the drivers from whose bus prospective members of the National Youths Service Corps, NYSC, were kidnapped on October 1, has told the court he was unaware that two of his passengers had AK-47 rifles in a bag. Read Also: NYSC kidnap: DSS witness exposes how suspects were identified The Department of State Services, DSS, on Friday, called two witnesses in the ongoing suit, HOU/22C/2026, filed against Usman Aliyu, Mohamed Aliyu and Babangida Ali, over the kidnap of 20 prospective NYSC members. The graduates were travelling to their orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. Led in evidence by the Principal State Counsel, Mr. Ekezie Nwauzor, the second prosecution witness, PW2, a commercial motorcyclist, Mr. Light Timothy, gave a graphic account of how the first and second accused persons hired him to take them to where their colleagues were staying. According to PW2, his two passengers were carrying a bag, which he never knew the content until they reached their lonely destination, where AK-47 rifles were brought out from it. He recalled that when his passenger put a call to someone, his intonation sounded Hausa or Fulani and the fellow urged him to ply the Umuguma-Okuku Road in Owerri West Local Government Area of Imo State. PW2 also told the court that at a point, fear gripped him and he wanted to go back but not long after, four men jumped out of the bush, collected the bag, opened it and brought out the AK-47 rifles. Timothy also told the court that he would have been killed for wasting time on the road, if not that one of them pleaded on his behalf and he sped off from that point. In his own evidence, the third prosecution witness, PW3, and Akwa Ibom Transport Company driver, Mr. Sunday Udoh, confirmed that he and another driver, Jeremiah, were carrying NYSC members from Ibadan, to their orientation camps. They had a stopover at Onitsha and left 5.30am on October 1, 2026, adding that heading towards Owerri and not long after passing a checkpoint, he noticed two stationary mini buses. He told the court that on sensing looming danger and he quickly tried to reverse but his vehicle hit something behind and they were stuck. According to Udoh, he switched off his vehicle, ran to the other side of the highway, hid in the nearby bush and watched events from there. Udoh, after identifying Usman Aliyu as one of the attackers, also said that the kidnappers took away five of his passengers and 15 from Jeremiah’s bus, into the bush. After thorough cross-examination of the two witnesses by the defence counsel, Paschal Ofoma, Justice Emeka Orafu adjourned the matter for further hearing to November 3, 2026. Meanwhile, a perusal through the list showed that nothing changed with the leadership of the Campaign Council. There were mainly additions to the membership cadre and minor housekeeping. item.title: Atiku accuses INEC of shielding officials behind voter register fraud
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of concealing evidence and shielding officials implicated in irregularities in the voter register, warning that the scandal threatens the credibility of the 2027 general elections. Atiku said INEC’s admission that AI-generated images and other irregularities had entered the register through registration officers exposed a grave failure of leadership and safeguards at the electoral body, raising fresh questions about the integrity of the database on which millions of Nigerians depend to exercise their franchise. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded the identification and prosecution of officials involved, full disclosure of evidence and an independent forensic audit of the voter register. He described INEC’s explanation of how the register was compromised as an attempt to evade responsibility. “That is a disgraceful evasion, not an answer. Even ordinary WhatsApp, Facebook and email accounts appear to have stronger security safeguards than those INEC’s ICT director described on national television. How can the database holding the votes of millions of Nigerians be less secure than a personal social media account?” he asked. Atiku said the Commission must disclose how the register was compromised, identify every officer involved and explain why those implicated had not been suspended or prosecuted. “Amupitan cannot admit the misconduct, withhold the perpetrators’ identities and expect Nigerians to accept ignorance as an excuse. He must account for this failure now,” he said. The former vice president also demanded an independent forensic audit, citing allegations that more than 20 million AI-generated images may have been involved. He warned against any attempt by INEC to quietly remove disputed records without preserving evidence of how the irregularities occurred. “Preserve every voter record, image file, access log and audit trail. Let accredited independent experts, political parties, civil society and credible international observers examine the evidence. No disputed record should be certified until the audit is complete,” he said. Atiku further accused INEC of ignoring opposition parties’ demand for disclosure of companies contracted to produce sensitive election materials, insisting that secrecy over the contractors and their operating protocols was incompatible with a credible election. He demanded that the Commission publish the contractors’ identities and explain the safeguards governing their work, arguing that opposition parties deserved the same information available to the APC-led Federal Government. item.title: Senegal kicks off Youth Games, Africa’s first ever Olympics
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, open Saturday in the Senegalese capital marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are abundant across Dakar, which is hosting some 2,665 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event marks the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “We’ve got people from around the world that maybe had a very different idea about Africa and they’re going to leave, hopefully, with something really positive in mind”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Thursday during a press conference in Dakar. “I think that is really important for our continent”, she said. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. – Sports culture – An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The west African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics have struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship. “Once the youth Olympic Games in Senegal begin, Dakar will become the capital of African youth,” Senegal Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said in an interview with AFP this week. “Africa hosting the (Youth) Olympic Games, it’s a symbol”, he said. – Russian athletes – With the IOC effectively lifting the Russian Olympic Committee’s (ROC) suspension in July, the Youth Games will mark the first Olympic competition since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 in which Russian athletes are allowed to compete under their own flag and colours. According to the ROC, 13 Russian athletes will participate and 10 coaches will accompany them to Senegal. “The kids are excited, it’s good news that our legitimate right to participate with the national anthem and Russian flag has been restored”, Anzor Gaunov, who coaches Anastasia Dobrovolskaya in judo, told AFP earlier this month in Moscow. item.title: US judge issues restraining order against Justice Dept over election directives
item.description: A US federal judge temporarily blocked on Friday the Justice Department from threatening state and local election officials with criminal prosecution if they fail to comply with its directives on processing ballots. The order by Judge Trina Thompson in the Northern District of California deals a setback to Trump administration efforts to restrict voting by people it says might not be US citizens in the November 3 midterm elections. The harshly worded temporary restraining order was issued in response to a case brought by labor union and civil rights groups against the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security. “Defendants shall not threaten, intimidate or coerce state or local elections officials or workers to demand that they halt processing the ballots of any registered voter solely on the basis that the ballot belongs to an individual alleged by Defendants to be ineligible to vote,” Thompson wrote. The judge also ruled that Justice Department officials “shall not threaten state or local election officials and workers with criminal prosecution for failure to comply” with such demands. President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is at risk of losing its control of Congress in next Tuesday’s elections, and critics have accused his administration of trying to cast doubt on electoral results. On Wednesday, a federal judge rejected the Justice Department’s efforts to set aside the ballots of more than 20,000 California voters it said might not be citizens, slamming the move as brazen pre-election “interference.” In Friday’s ruling, Thompson said that a restraining order, which expires on November 16, was justified “given the fast-approaching date of the Election” and because the plaintiffs “have demonstrated that they will likely succeed on the merits of their claims.” Thompson described the “intimidation” and threats of criminal prosecution of election workers as “contrary to law” and “arbitrary and capricious.” In a wide-ranging order, the judge said the defendants shall not demand the removal of specific registered voters from voter lists, nor refuse to issue ballots to specific voters nor demand ballots not be counted because of alleged ineligibility to vote. For months, Trump — who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Joe Biden in 2020 — has been claiming that there will be fraud in this year’s midterms. Studies repeatedly show that while rare cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are minuscule and do not influence US election results. item.title: Police confirm rescue of 3 kidnapped Zamfara Islamic clerics
item.description: The Zamfara Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Bello, has confirmed the rescue of three of the six Islamic Clerics (Imam) kidnapped on September 12, while travelling to Talata Mafara, Zamfara. Bello gave the confirmation in an interview with some select reporters on Friday in Gusau. He said the rescue followed a multi-agency collaboration and seamless synergy between the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), the Department of State Services (DSS) and police operatives. The CP said security tactical operations remained ongoing in full force, leveraging real-time intelligence supplied by local community members to track down the remaining armed bandits and ensure the safe rescue of the three clerics still in captivity. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the ONSA, in a high-stakes intelligence-driven collaboration with the DSS and the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), rescued the three Islamic clerics kidnapped while en route to a special prayer session for President Bola Tinubu in Talata Mafara, Zamfara. NAN also reports that the victims were part of a group of six Islamic clerics abducted on Sept. 12, when heavily armed bandits intercepted them around 11:30 a.m. on the Dakko-Damri feeder road near Sububu Forest in Bakura Local Government Area. The clerics, identified as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam Bala Fagon and Na’ibi Tasi’u, were travelling to Talata Mafara to attend a special prayer gathering to seek divine favour for Tinubu’s administration. Their abductors had reportedly demanded N30 million ransom for their release. A senior security operative involved in the extraction also confirmed that the three clerics were rescued unhurt following meticulous, intelligence-led manoeuvres. NAN learnt that the clerics are said to be in stable condition after receiving medical evaluation and expert debriefing. The security operatives confirmed that the three clerics were slated for formal handover to the Zamfara Government to reunite them with their families. The Police command assured that operational leads would continue, urging the public to maintain a vigilant flow of timely, actionable information to help flush out terrorist elements across the region. item.title: Sowore, police differ over attack in Ekiti
item.description: Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and the Ekiti State Police Command have given conflicting accounts of an incident at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday. While Sowore insisted that he and members of his team were violently attacked, the police described the incident as an altercation with some individuals, saying the activist sustained a minor injury. The Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, said the command received an alert that Sowore was having issues with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti and immediately deployed operatives to the scene. Abutu said the operatives rescued the AAC presidential candidate and took him to the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti, where he was receiving treatment. However, Sowore, in a statement published on his social media accounts, rejected the police description of the incident as an “altercation”. “There was no altercation! We were attacked!” he declared. He accused the Ekiti State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) of attempting to suppress evidence relating to the incident. Sowore alleged that security operatives seized CCTV footage from the restaurant where the incident occurred, claiming that the attackers were captured on camera and accusing the agencies of attempting to shield those responsible. He also faulted the state Commissioner of Police, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, for describing the incident as an altercation, saying the police commissioner had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but subsequently played down their severity. Sowore further alleged that DSS operatives had been trailing and harassing him since his arrival in the state on Thursday. He claimed that the operatives also threatened the manager of a restaurant where he and his team had earlier eaten, warning him against allowing them to use the premises again. He said the attack occurred shortly after he concluded an interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 in Ado-Ekiti on Friday. Sowore also alleged that some of the attackers came from the Ekiti State Government House and received operational support from DSS operatives. Police Response The police, however, denied reports that the activist was kidnapped, following a social media post claiming that he had been seized by armed thugs and his whereabouts were unknown. Abutu said in a statement that the command wished to clarify that Sowore was not kidnapped but was rescued by police operatives after they received information about the incident. “The command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, following which the police were immediately alerted. “Upon receiving the report, police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. item.title: Some called him warlord, but he was liberator, pan-Africanist – Yormie Johnson’s widow
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Speaking about Liberia’s democratic evolution without mentioning the late Prince Yormie Johnson, better known as PYJ, would be a disservice to history. Although Johnson died on November 28, 2024, at the age of 72, he transitioned from being an officer in the Armed Forces of Liberia to becoming a democrat, senator and two-time presidential candidate. Hailing from Nimba County, the second-most populous county in Liberia, Johnson wielded considerable influence over the county’s politics, operating as a key kingmaker and political deal-broker. His support was instrumental in the emergence of presidents. His political protégé is the current Vice President of Liberia, Jeremiah Kpan Koung Sr. In this exclusive interview, the late PYJ’s widow, Mrs Amira Johnson, during a recent visit to Nigeria, shares insights into life without her husband, and struggles for the liberation of his people, describing him as a pan-Africanist. She also calls on African leaders to remain united in the interest of the continent. Excerpts: How has your experience been so far, and what has impressed you most about the country since your arrival? Well, Nigeria is like a second home to me and my family. If you could recall, my husband and I settled here briefly during the time of the crisis in Liberia. My husband was moved here by the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, and we stayed here and nurtured our children for 14 years. When the political atmosphere became stable, we had to go back and my husband contested to be a senator. So, my experience here has been so wonderful. Before now, I had come, but since my husband passed, this is my first time coming. Also, I came to SCOAN, which is my major reason for coming. I came to meet with the woman of God, Pastor Mrs TB Joshua. She and the late prophet TB Joshua had been our spiritual parents before my husband passed. While we lived in Nigeria for 14 years, that was where we used to fellowship and we went back to Liberia where we used to come from time to time. But since the prophet passed away and my husband passed on, this is my first experience. It has been wonderful. She received me warmly at the church. She hosted me. She is like a family. She welcomed me and we spent quality time visiting the mountains, doing spiritual work, praying for Liberia, praying for myself, my family and for peace and stability in the world in general. Prophet TB Joshua died five years ago. Given that you had not visited SCOAN since his passing, did you notice any change about the church? I must admit, I was quite impressed with the church. item.title: The Signal: INEC Draws The Line, The Politicians Must Now Face The Voters
item.description: An important decision on governorship candidates, fresh pressure over the voters’ register, and a new battle for the South-East have shifted the 2027 campaign into more consequential territory. The politicians are still negotiating power. The electoral commission is beginning to determine who can contest it. For weeks, Nigeria’s political conversation has revolved around familiar questions. Who is supporting President Bola Tinubu? Can Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi agree on a common strategy? How much influence does Nyesom Wike command? Which governor will deliver which state? Then, on Friday, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reminded everyone that there is another player in this election: the umpire. INEC announced the outcome of its review of complaints arising from the exclusion of governorship and state assembly candidates. Some politicians received welcome news. Others discovered that their appeals had failed. Among the most notable decisions, former Communications Minister Isa Pantami succeeded in his petition concerning the Gombe governorship election, although his candidacy remains subject to pending litigation. Ladi Adebutu, the PDP’s governorship candidate in Ogun State, was less fortunate. His petition was rejected. These decisions may appear to be administrative matters. They are not. They affect the choices available to voters, the calculations of political parties, and potentially the balance of power in important states. And they arrive at a moment when INEC is already facing intense scrutiny over the integrity of the voters’ register. The emerging question is no longer simply which politician has the strongest campaign organisation. It is whether Nigeria’s electoral institutions can apply the rules consistently, resolve disputes transparently and command public confidence when the votes are counted. Pantami gets a reprieve. Adebutu does not. INEC’s latest decisions offer a revealing picture of the difficulties political parties are experiencing with the Electoral Act and candidate nomination procedures. The commission received 69 petitions from 12 political parties across 26 states concerning governorship nominations. Of those, 41 succeeded, and 28 were rejected. For state assembly elections, 25 of the 61 petitions were successful, while 36 were rejected. The figures tell us something important. This is not an isolated disagreement involving one or two politicians. It is a substantial problem affecting party nominations across the country. The disputes concern membership registers, compliance with statutory deadlines, alleged multiple nominations and the wrongful inclusion or exclusion of candidates. INEC says it examined the complaints against relevant records and legal provisions. In Gombe, Pantami’s successful petition offers the PDP an opportunity to compete with a candidate whose exclusion had threatened its position in the state. But the pending court proceedings mean that the matter is not entirely settled

item.title: 46-yr-old businessman commits suicide, leaves video message for family
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure A 46-year-old businessman, Akinbolusere Kayode, has reportedly died by suicide in Ondo Town, Ondo State. Sources said he took his life in his office near BOVAS Petrol Station in Igba Town at about 3 p.m. on Thursday. Two empty bottles suspected to have contained poisonous substance were recovered by police detectives attached to the Bolorunduro Division who visited the scene. According to sources, the deceased recorded a video in which he spoke about his business challenges, humble beginnings, and relationship with his wife, whom he praised for standing by him throughout his struggles. He also repeatedly stated that no one pressured him into deciding to transfer his properties to his wife and three children. The state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, confirmed the incident. Abayomi said the two empty bottles suspected to have contained Sniper insecticide were recovered from a nearby bush during the police investigation. He added that preliminary findings indicated that the deceased recorded a video before his death in which he lamented the hardships he faced in life. The video has since circulated widely on social media. His remains were evacuated and deposited at the State Hospital morgue for preservation and further examination. Police said no signs of foul play or visible injuries were observed on the body during the initial examination. The Commissioner of Police in the state, Felix Ohagwu, has ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident to determine the actual cause of death. Ohagwu urged members of the public to refrain from speculation and allow investigators to carry out their work. He also advised individuals experiencing emotional distress, marital difficulties, or other personal challenges to seek timely support and assistance rather than resorting to actions that could endanger their lives. item.title: ‘Why I strangled, mutilated Adedotun Oluwaseun’ – Murder suspect who mourned with victim’s family
item.description: By Evelyn Usman For the family of Mrs Adedotun Oluwaseun, retirement was supposed to usher in a season of peace, rest and the joy of reaping the fruits of years of dedicated service. Instead, the death of their beloved mother has left them grieving and grappling with painful questions about the circumstances surrounding her final hours. A home that should have offered her security became the scene of a violent death, leaving her family searching for answers. Nearly eight months after the incident, the Ogun State Police Command announced a breakthrough with the arrest of 49-year-old Saburi Lateef, a popular transporter in Abeokuta, also known as Alhaji Oki Osan. In a disturbing twist, the suspect was reportedly among those who visited the deceased’s residence to commiserate with her family after her death, according to police sources. Investigation A source in the Homicide Section of the Ogun State Police Command, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said investigators initially had no clear lead to the perpetrator. According to the source: “At the beginning, there was no link to the perpetrator of the act, but the Commissioner of Police, CP Olubode Ojajuni, directed that we should ensure that we do everything possible to unravel the killers.” Police sources alleged that Lateef gained access to the deceased’s residence while she was away attending a retirement party organised for a friend around the Rounder area of Abeokuta. “He was ransacking the whole place when the woman returned. In his bid to prevent being exposed, he strangled the woman. “Not convinced that the woman was dead, he picked a cutlass and inflicted multiple cuts on her body. After that, he picked up her body and took it to the toilet, where he placed it on the closet to confirm if she was actually dead. “He spent more than an hour carrying out the act without attracting the attention of other residents in the neighbourhood,” the source alleged. ‘I don’t know what came over me’ — Suspect In his account, Lateef attributed his alleged action to frustration over the money he claimed Oluwaseun was keeping for him. item.title: ‘I cry, break down behind closed doors’ – Funke Akindele reflects on pressures of being in the spotlight
item.description: By Aiyedun Oluwadamilola Nollywood actress and producer Funke Akindele has opened up about her emotional struggles behind the cameras, revealing that she sometimes cries and breaks down in private despite her cheerful public image. The actress made this known during an interview with CNN, where she reflected on the pressures of fame, public scrutiny of her relationships and the importance of prioritising personal well-being. “I cry. I lock myself in the room, cry, break down, and hit the bed. But I just pick myself up and come back to life,” Akindele said. The filmmaker, popularly associated with her ability to entertain audiences through her films and public appearances, acknowledged that the cheerful image people see does not always reflect what she experiences privately. She also spoke about the effect of public opinion on her personal life, recalling moments when she questioned her decisions and worried about how people would judge her. “Sometimes I tell myself, you’ve made a mistake again. How are people going to judge you?” she said, describing the thoughts she sometimes had to overcome. Akindele explained that she has gradually learnt to confront challenges and move forward rather than allow public opinion to determine how she sees herself. Beyond dealing with criticism, the actress highlighted the importance of self-care and maintaining relationships with loved ones while pursuing professional success. item.title: Taraba: Day bandits killed 62, injured 52, dislodged 7,123
item.description: • We can no longer farm, they took everything away from us — survivor By Femi Bolaji, Jalingo Friday, October 23, 2026, began like any other market day in Binnari, a rural community in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, where the life of the people revolves around farming, fishing, livestock rearing and cross border trade. Read Also: Death toll in Taraba bandits’ attack now 50 From the early hours, residents and traders from neighbouring communities were busy going about their daily activities. Farmers brought their produce to market, food sellers prepared for customers, and livestock owners hoped to make sales that would help sustain their families. For many, the market was more than a place to buy and sell. It was where household needs were met, school fees were raised, debts were settled and plans for the coming week were made. But before the day ended, that familiar routine had been violently interrupted. Armed bandits on motorbikes reportedly stormed the community, opening fire on people going about their business, killing residents, destroying property and looting stores. In the confusion that followed, families fled for safety, leaving behind homes, belongings and livelihoods they had spent years building. By the time the immediate danger had passed, Binnari had been left counting its losses. Casualties The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), in it’s preliminary reports from the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA) and posted on its official social media handles put the death toll at 62. Another 52 people were reported injured, while 5,187 residents were displaced and 7,123 people affected by the attack. The figures, contained in a statement issued by NEMA on October 27, 2026, followed an on-the-spot assessment by TSEMA’s Executive Secretary, Dr. Echuseh Audu. Behind those numbers are families struggling to understand how a day that began with ordinary hopes ended in death, displacement and uncertainty. For the people of Binnari, the tragedy is not simply about the number of lives lost. It is also about the children whose education may have been interrupted, the farmers who have lost their livestock, the traders who can no longer return to the market with confidence and the families now wondering how to begin again. In a community where people depend largely on what they produce, catch, rear or sell, the attack has threatened not only lives but the very means through which residents survive. Binnari’s market has long served as an important meeting point for people from different communities and neighbouring states like Plateau, Gombe and Bauchi. Farmers come with grain and other agricultural produce. Fishermen bring their catch, while livestock owners and traders gather to exchange goods and negotiate prices. item.title: Masussuka: Life, preaching, death
item.description: The murder of Katsina-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, has stirred emotions and sparked conversations around the life and times of a popular preacher seen through different lenses. To his army of followers, he embodied peace, dignity and tolerance for religious differences. To his critics, he was a controversial scholar whose religious ideology and preaching were questionable. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, on Monday evening in front of his house at Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in an attack claimed by the extremist group, Ansaru. Amnesty International has called on the Nigerian government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. Masussuka: We reject his ideology but condemn his killing – JIBWIS Imam Masussuka’s preaching, killing contrary to Islamic laws – Sheikh Maraya The 47-year-old cleric subscribed to and preached Quranic teachings, but, to greater extent, disregarded Hadith, the sayings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) – a stance that placed him at variance with his critics. He alleged that a lot of Hadiths being attributed to the Prophet were not from him, saying they were concocted by some people out of mischief. Masussuka reportedly began preaching at the tender age of 13 and rose to prominence with the advent of social media, through which he established himself as one of the most vocal clerics among the Qur’aniyun Islamic sect. Through his active social media platforms, his preaching gained more recognition, increasingly attracting attention from other sects with different ideologies. Masussuka’s increased visibility drew controversies around his ideology. One major controversy surrounding Masussuka’s teachings and ideology revolved around his rejection of certain Hadith traditions as authorities and forms of religious practice. According to other sects, his doctrine that only the Qur’an serves as the gateway to religious practice goes contrary to a larger belief that both the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet are central sources of Islamic guidance. Disagreements over his ideology became more pronounced and his teachings were challenged on several occasions. Though disagreement on the interpretation and authority of Hadith has long existed among Muslim scholars, Masussuka’s unique stance on the matter placed him at odds with scholars who considered his teachings inconsistent with established Islamic traditions. Amid growing scrutiny of his preaching, the Katsina State Government, on November 18, 2025, announced that Masussuka would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars established based on the several calls. The meeting, however, didn’t see the light of day due to undisclosed circumstances, as he continued to challenge other sects that go against his ideologies. item.title: Parallel campaigns within APC
item.description: While the All Progressives Congress (APC) officially kicked off its presidential campaign last week, a major hindrance to its effective spread in all the geopolitical zones and states in the country has remained the lack of synergy in many states. Weekend Trust checks revealed that there are many states where leaders of the party claiming to work for the reelection of its presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, prefer to work in isolated camps, without as much as involving other leaders in its operations. This, our correspondent learnt, is due to unresolved leadership disputes, personality clashes and the bid outdo each other to prove the one with the bigger political worth. The intensity, however, varies in degree from state to state, with some openly defying each other, while some put up a façade of working together, but beneath the surface are trying to undermine each other’s efforts. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Nigeria’s drug battle Investigations reveal that in states where the governors joined the APC only after winning elections, the process of integrating the party structure on ground has not been concluded, leading to suspicion between those who moved the governors and those they met on ground. In states like Plateau, Taraba, Adamawa and Kano, there are still vestiges of animosity between the two major camps of the defecting governors and those they met on ground. In states like Anambra and Osun, where the governors are members of other parties but have been integrated into the APC presidential campaign council, the preexisting party structures there have shown that they are not comfortable with the arrangement. States like Benue, Ondo, Katsina, Zamfara have shown that the contending forces are not aligned to work together for the reelection bid of its presidential candidate due to unrestrained rivalries between the governors and other powerful figures from the party in their states, who have the ears of Abuja. Our correspondents capture what is going on in some of the states. Masari, who is considered one of the influential APC figures in Katsina, was absent during the inauguration of the Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda. He was also missing at the official flag-off of the campaign in Funtua Local Government Area. However, rather than joining the governor at the public campaign events, Masari is said to have intensified separate political consultations within and outside Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Nigeria’s drug battle
item.description: Despite massive seizures, arrest of Nigerians and foreign nationals, prosecution and dismantling of clandestine methamphetamine laboratories linked to international criminal networks by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), among others, drug trafficking remains a major challenge in Nigeria. From industrial-scale drug production to cocaine couriers and cross-border syndicates, the persistence of the illicit trade raises questions about the sophistication of criminal networks and the factors sustaining the business. The growing drug problem has continued to impact negatively on the health and general wellbeing of many Nigerians, especially the youth population. Many families and households note that they are going through a lot of trauma and pains in the management and rehabilitation of their children and loved ones who have become victims of drug addiction. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Parallel campaigns within APC According to data from the NDLEA, over the last five years, a total of 96,157 suspects, including 250 drug barons, have been arrested; 15, 833, 856.3kgs of illicit drug seized with 2,099.96 hectares of cannabis farms destroyed. Within the same period, the agency secured 18,691 convictions while 54, 517 were counselled and rehabilitated. Between January 2026 and September 2026 alone, data showed that 18,290 arrests have been made with illicit drug seizures of 698,488.76kgs while 81.69 hectares of cannabis farms have been destroyed across the country. Within the same period, a total of 2,568 convictions were recorded while 5,681 were counselled and rehabilitated. The agency has also recorded the dismantling of four industrial meth laboratories across four states in recent months. Besides the destructions of meth laboratories, international drug traffickers, including those from South Africa and other parts of the world, have also been arrested in recent months, with some already facing prosecution. The agency also announced drug recoveries across several states, including Lagos, Kano, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta, anong others. Notwithstanding the massive seizures, arrests, convictions and destruction of illicit drugs by the agency, the drug trafficking challenge remains potent, with experts saying that Nigeria is not just a transit route for illicit drug but also evolving as a production hub. In this report, Weekend Trust examines some of the factors making Nigeria a drug trafficking destination and production hub, impacts on drug users and abusers, nexus between drug trafficking and insecurity, and the way forward. item.title: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma
item.description: •Court grants Okorocha ticket, 12 Chairmen back go vernor By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The fight over who flies the All Progressives Congress (APC) flag in Imo West Senatorial District has turned into open war, with the party’s 12 local government chairmen in the zone rejecting a court judgment that handed the ticket to former Governor Rochas Okorocha and insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains the candidate. State APC chairman, Austin Onyedebelu spoke on behalf of the Chairmen. Said he: “We reject this judgment in its entirety because it is an undisguised travesty of justice. It is a political robbery clothed in legal robes, the latest instalment of a satanic scheme hatched by Abuja politicians against the South-East,” the chairmen declared. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled on Thursday that Okorocha, and not the governor, won the party’s May 18 primary for the district. He held that Okorocha had produced “sufficient evidence” that he won the exercise, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Court order The court ordered the APC to forward Okorocha’s name to INEC and directed the commission to publish him as the party’s validly nominated candidate. It also barred Uzodimma from presenting himself as the APC candidate in the election. The chairmen said they were in the field on May 18, 2026, when the primary was held, and that Okorocha scored only 1,098 votes against about 230,000 for Uzodimma, who was declared winner in the presence of INEC staff. “For the avoidance of doubt, we NEVER VOTED FOR ROCHAS OKOROCHA,” Onyedebelu said. “This legal somersault orchestrated by enemies of Ndigbo was obviously procured not only to destabilise Orlu zone but to consolidate the war of attrition by some Nigerians to politically hold down the south east.” They said Okorocha never used the window provided by the party to petition its appeal panel over any irregularity, only to go to court and be handed victory. The chairmen pointed to what they called wild celebrations by Okorocha since Thursday and his remarks that he got help from higher quarters outside the court. In their view, this showed a conspiracy to shut Ndigbo out of political relevance. They said they were enraged that people outside Igboland wanted to use Okorocha as an errand boy to supplant the wish of the majority of APC members in the Orlu zone, who overwhelmingly voted for Uzodimma. “Our grievance lies with a small circle of power brokers who appear determined that no Igbo man shall come close to the first, second, or third positions in the land. item.title: ‘Northern leaders begged Tinubu to support Buhari, promised to return power after eight years’ – APC chieftain
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, APC, and former House of Representative member representing Birnin-Kudu/ Buji in Jigawa State, Engr. Magaji Da’u Aliyu, has claimed that Northern political leaders begged President Bola Tinubu to support former President Muhammadu Buhari’s presidential ambition and promised to return power to his side after eight years. ‎Aliyu, who is also the Deputy Campaign Director of the North for Tinubu Support Group, disclosed this while addressing supporters in Birnin Kudu. ‎He said the North has no justification for opposing Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 general election, insisting that the region must honour the political agreement allegedly reached before Buhari became president in 2015. ‎ ‎According to him, Buhari had contested the presidential election three times without success before Northern political leaders approached Tinubu in Lagos to seek his support. ‎ ‎”Buhari contested the presidential election three times and lost. We then went to Lagos to beg Tinubu to support Buhari’s presidential ambition,” he said. ‎ ‎”He agreed to support us on the understanding that after Buhari’s eight years in office, power would return to his side, and we accepted the agreement.” ‎ ‎Aliyu maintained that supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 is a matter of honouring the promise made to him, stressing that Northerners have no reason to abandon the agreement. ‎ ‎”For every Northerner, fulfilling that agreement is mandatory. We have no reason not to honour the agreement we entered into,” he said. ‎ ‎The APC chieftain pledged that members of the Northern Tinubu Support Group would commit their resources towards ensuring the President’s victory in the next presidential election. ‎ ‎”On our part, we will support Tinubu’s re-election bid with our lives and wealth to ensure that we fulfil the promise we made,” he added. ‎ ‎Speaking on insecurity, Aliyu also defended President Tinubu against criticism over the country’s security challenges. ‎ ‎He argued that no human being has absolute power to guarantee security, insisting that only God can provide lasting peace and stability. ‎ ‎”Let us stop the blame game. Only God has the power to provide security. We should seek His forgiveness, and He will grant us peace and stability,” he said. item.title: ‘Debt worse than leprosy’ – Obasanjo tackles Tinubu
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity. The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”. Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn. “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he sa

item.title: Drunk barber allegedly stabs man to death in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested a 29-year-old barber, Emmanuel Olatonok, for allegedly stabbing a 32-year-old man, Ibrahim Shago, to death while reportedly under the influence of alcohol. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists. The incident occurred on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at about 5:45 p.m. in the Rafin Sanyi area of Dutse Local Government Area. According to the police spokesperson, the suspect, who reportedly worked as a barber at a hotel in Dutse, allegedly stabbed the victim in the neck with a knife following an argument. He added that the suspect was allegedly under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. “The suspect, a barber reportedly working at a popular hotel in Dutse, allegedly stabbed the victim in the neck with a knife following an argument,” he said. Adam explained that the victim, a resident of Karnaya town, was immediately rushed to a hospital for medical attention but was later confirmed dead by a medical doctor. He said the incident triggered tension in the area as some angry youths gathered at the scene and attempted to vandalise the hotel. However, police operatives from Dutse Division quickly intervened and brought the situation under control, preventing further violence and destruction of property. The police spokesperson confirmed that the suspect is currently in custody, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing. He added that the suspect would be charged to court upon the conclusion of the investigation. item.title: 21 cars affected as fire engulfs Lagos mechanic workshop
item.description: By Evelyn Usman A mechanic workshop went up in flames in the early hours of yesterday at Isheri-Idimu, Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State, with 21 vehicles reportedly affected. The fire, which broke out at about 3:05am on Oladunni Street, beside Eternal Filling Station, reportedly threatened to spread to the adjoining petrol station, raising fears of a possible major disaster, according to eyewitnesses. However, the swift intervention of emergency responders reportedly prevented the inferno from spreading to the filling station and nearby buildings. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said its Dolphin Response Team, stationed at Igando, was immediately activated following a distress call. The Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, said: “Upon arrival, responders discovered that the fire had engulfed a mechanical workshop where several exotic vehicles were parked, in close proximity to a petroleum filling station. Through the prompt, professional and coordinated intervention of the LASEMA Response Team and the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, supported by the Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and the Nigeria Police Force, the inferno was prevented from spreading to the filling station and surrounding structures, thereby averting what could have been a major disaster. “The fire has been completely extinguished and damping-down operations concluded. Preliminary assessment indicates that about twenty-one (21) exotic vehicles were affected, with a section of a nearby building sustaining minor damage. “Importantly, no loss of life and no injury were recorded. “The Lagos State Government, through LASEMA, reiterates its commitment to the protection of lives and property across the state. The agency commends the bravery and diligence of all responders whose swift action ensured that the incident was brought under control without casualties. “Members of the public are enjoined to continue to prioritise safety measures, particularly in workshops and environments where inflammable materials are handled, and to promptly alert emergency services through the toll-free emergency numbers 767 and 112 in the event of any emergency,” he said. item.title: Debt Worse Than Leprosy, Destroys Generations, Says Obasanjo
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his position on borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because it destroys generations. He stated this while speaking at a symposium, a public forum focused on leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate national development in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Tinubu had said in April that borrowing should not be viewed negatively, insisting that the government would borrow when necessary, provided it could repay the loans. President Bola Tinubu (Photo: X@aonanuga1956) But Obasanjo disagreed, describing such a position as absolute nonsense. The former president also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance, recalling that when he established his farm 47 years ago, the naira exchanged at ₦1 to $1 and 85 cents. He challenged the country’s leadership to explain the naira’s depreciation to about ₦1,500 to a dollar, questioning what Nigeria had achieved over the decades. Meanwhile, the guest speaker, historian and public policy scholar, Umar Ardo, has warned that artificial intelligence could deepen Africa’s dependence on foreign powers if the continent fails to control its technology and digital infrastructure. Ardo warned that without investments in chip fabrication, data centres, African-owned datasets and continental cooperation, artificial intelligence could become another tool for managing Africa rather than empowering the continent to determine its own future. Amid criticism, President Tinubu on Thursday defended his administration’s plan to take more foreign loans , arguing that Nigeria needs long-term investment in infrastructure to achieve its ambition of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2030. The President said the proposed loans would be used to build roads, improve electricity supply, upgrade ports and fund other projects that would create jobs, grow businesses and provide opportunities for future generations. In a statement titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” Tinubu said the focus should be on what the borrowed money would achieve rather than how much the government was borrowing. “The key question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, the value we create and the future we leave behind,” he said. He listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid improvements and upgrades to major commercial ports in Lagos among the projects the government plans to fund. He said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce the cost of transporting goods, support farming and industries, and attract private investors. The President said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway alone could reduce transport costs along its route by 15 to 20 per cent and add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) through increased trade, tourism
